RES-2024-175 was adopted November 12, 2024 and took effect 60 days later (about January 11, 2025); the pilot ends three years after the effective date (about January 2028) or on adoption of a new CFF nexus study, whichever is first. The zero fee for the Low Income category stops once the City reaches its RHNA Low Income unit total. The 2026 Prohousing renewal application (source) describes the CFF pilot and streamlined design review for 100% affordable projects but does not state a 50 percent permit fee reduction, so that claim is unconfirmed. The CFF for a multifamily unit is several thousand dollars, so the waiver is worth roughly $100,000 to $500,000 on a typical project (confirm with the current fee schedule).
